synthesis.answer: Intermittent fasting can lead to modest weight loss compared with eating as usual [99b6719a4d98#0]. Most of that loss appears to come from eating fewer calories overall [f1bc00eaa754#1]. When calories are matched, fasting does not beat ordinary calorie restriction in longer trials [434ee86bde79#1] [291da337f819#0]. Drop-out is higher on strict schedules, which may explain why results vary [4cceb5c4db62#0]. Fasting is not suitable for everyone and people on medication should check with a clinician [67a050ff68a6#0]. Overall, it is a reasonable option for people who find it easy to follow, but the evidence does not show it is better than other plans.
synthesis.one_line: Works about as well as other calorie-cutting plans, not better.
